notes: The San Francisco City Planning Commission's minutes of its meetings of 1995, from volume 41 of the San Francisco Public Library's deposit at the Internet Archive (41minutesofsanfran1995san). Action minutes, as in 1994: each calendar item prints its case number and planner, the property with its assessor's block and lot, the request, the speakers by name, and the action with the vote and the motion or resolution number. Pages were split from the hOCR search text on the Internet Archive page index (whose first two fields are the text offsets), counting the viewer page among the leaves scandata.xml does not mark addToAccessFormats=false, and every page is dated from the meeting header it sits under. Four kinds of finding: what the Commission decided about a property, dated to the meeting that decided it; what the calendar states stood on or occupied the property; and landmark actions. A continuance, a withdrawal, a motion of intent or an item under 'Items to be continued' is not a decision. The minutes name applicants, owners, architects, neighbours, objectors, commissioners and staff in every item; none of them is in any field. Companies, institutions, businesses and named buildings are kept.

coverage.remaining: Every page of volume 41 (41minutesofsanfran1995san, labelled 1995) was read: 43 meeting days, 9 January to 14 December 1995, including the special meeting of 9 January, the joint hearings with the Recreation and Park Commission of 4 May and 28 September, and the field-trip minutes of 2 March, 22 June and 7 July. The volume holds no minutes for 16 February, 23 March, 26 October or 2 November 1995 (the first and the last two are adopted at later meetings); 1 June, 31 August, 23 November and 21 December were cancelled; 17 August is bound twice (n206-n213 and n214-n221) and the first copy is cited. Next: volumes 42-58 (1996-2005).
coverage.note: 327 OCR pages with text out of 350 viewer pages (352 scanned leaves; the empty ones are blank versos, the library cards and the digitization notice), read in one session by a single reader with no sub-agents. The year of the Residential Conservation Amendments and their interim controls, of the Hayes Valley and Yerba Buena Plaza East public housing rebuilds, of the Tier III calendar of rear additions, of four theatre landmarks (Brown's Opera House, El Capitan, the Columbarium, the Alhambra initiated) and the York Theater's eligibility finding, and of the Pier 39 Ferris wheel.
